A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same navigation framework, renamed from P3Nav to RoboTron-Nav. All 14 pages of each version, including supplementary text, equations, tables, and qualitative figures, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original ObjectNav performance, ObjectNavRoom ablations, hyperparameter experiments, and qualitative navigation trajectories.

after.justification: V2 reports original navigation results and ablations, including additional semantic-threshold experiments and training-efficiency observations.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 adds a semantic-similarity threshold: spatially nearby observations are discarded only when their cosine similarity also exceeds the threshold. This allows different viewpoints at nearby positions to survive. The change refines the existing sampler while retaining the visual architecture, positional encoding, multitask training, output heads, and losses.

E1.justification: Both versions use CHORES-S ObjectNav, ObjectNavRoom, and their generated EQA training pairs. The dataset sizes, represented environments, navigation tasks, and qualitative scenarios are retained. Additional cited datasets and descriptions of baseline capabilities do not constitute new evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 expands the comparator set from EmbSigLIP, SPOC, and SPOC* to also include PIRLNav, JSRL, and RING. This substantially broadens the competitive comparison, adding imitation-plus-reinforcement-learning approaches and a stronger comparator: RING reports 72.1 SR and 53.0 SEL.

E3.justification: V2 introduces a semantic-threshold sweep at fixed W=60 and epsilon=0.1, adopts tau=0.95, and specifies the no-sampling control as epsilon=0 and tau=1. The evaluation split of 200 trajectories in 200 houses, metrics, dataset sizes, and stated five-epoch training budget remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 4 retains the original window-size and spatial-threshold experiments and adds three semantic-threshold settings. Supplementary Section 7.2.3 adds a brief training-cost and convergence comparison. Figure 7 reassigns the existing chair-case trajectories between methods; it does not introduce a new case.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without seed counts, repeated-run statistics, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V2's qualitative convergence-stability statement does not add statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: For the revised model on the retained ObjectNav benchmark, Table 1 changes SR/SEL/%Rooms from 75.0/34.3/69.4 to 81.1/43.9/67.8. Tables 2 and 3 also change proposed-model results, while Table 4 adds semantic-threshold outcomes. New baseline entries change the SEL leader to RING. Figure 7 reverses the chair-trajectory attribution between SPOC and the proposed method without explaining the reassignment.

T1.justification: The positional-encoding equations, constant-height assumption, training-loss formulations, and SEL formula are retained. Neither version introduces theorems, proofs, or theoretical guarantees. The new sampling condition changes the algorithm, while the expanded UVFormer description supplies implementation detail.

C1.justification: The unified perception/planning/prediction and navigation/EQA contributions remain. The sampling contribution now explicitly includes semantic diversity and different viewpoints at nearby positions. The headline SR changes from 75% to 81.1%, and the claimed absolute margin changes from 18 to 9 percentage points, with the latter matching the added RING comparison.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations linking excessive history, overly sparse spatial sampling, and semantic redundancy to performance degradation. It also attributes PIRLNav/JSRL performance to sparse-reward difficulties and discusses the multitask training-cost tradeoff. The existing simulation/generalization limitations remain. The retained 2.9-point PEHF ablation claim is inconsistent with revised Table 2, which implies 3.3 points.

D1.justification: V2 adds UVFormer grid/query details, a project-page link, an exact MPT checkpoint reference, and approximately doubled multitask training time. Its MPT identification replaces the earlier OpenFlamingo attribution without establishing whether the underlying backbone changed. V2 also removes the explicit statement that baseline scores were copied from original papers or supplementary materials.

R1.justification: V2 adds references and positioning for RING, PIRLNav, JSRL, and several embodied-AI or driving works, including DriveMM and DataPlatter. It removes the MultiON discussion/reference and the OpenFlamingo reference. These broaden contextual coverage without fundamentally changing the paper's research positioning.

P1.justification: The framework is renamed throughout, several introductory, related-work, method, and ablation paragraphs are streamlined, and explicit motivating questions and contribution bullets are added. Dataset details move into the supplement, which gains Section 7.2.3. The overall section sequence and narrative remain recognizable.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains comparator rows, and Table 4 gains a tau column and additional rows. Figure 2 and several tables are relocated within the layout, and figure labels reflect the renamed method. Figure 7 swaps the chair-case panels under the method labels. The existing figure set and overall two-column format are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the competitive comparison more informative by including RING, tests the added semantic threshold, and supplies useful implementation and training-cost details. These improve the paper's assessability beyond merely reporting higher scores. The benefit is limited by the stale Table 2 ablation claim, unexplained Figure 7 reassignment, and continued absence of uncertainty estimates; the PDFs do not establish whether the trajectory reassignment corrects an earlier error.
